item.title: Elder Vaṅgīsa: Sensual desire burns me! My mind is on fire. Good indeed, Gotama — Out of compassion, speak The Dhamma that extinguishes the blaze.…
item.description:
Elder Vaṅgīsa:

Sensual desire burns me!
My mind is on fire.
Good indeed, Gotama —
Out of compassion, speak
The Dhamma that extinguishes the blaze.

It is because of distorted perception
That your mind is on fire.
Abandon the sign of the beautiful
That leads to sensual desire.

See formations as impermanent,
Suffering, not-self —
Extinguish great sensual desire —
Do not be burned again and again.
Develop the mind on foulness,
One-pointed, well-concentrated.
Practice mindfulness of the body,
Practice much disenchantment.

Practice the signless,
Destroy the underlying tendency to conceit.
By thoroughly penetrating conceit,
Your practice will be at peace.

From: Theragāthā 21.1
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “So too, Māgandiya, if I were to teach you the Dhamma thus: ‘This is health, this is Nibbāna,’ you might know health and see Nibbāna.…
item.description:
“So too, Māgandiya, if I were to teach you the Dhamma thus: ‘This is health, this is Nibbāna,’ you might know health and see Nibbāna. And with the arising of the eye (of wisdom) in you, lust for the five aggregates of clinging would be abandoned, and you might think: ‘For a long time indeed I have been deceived, cheated, and fooled by this mind! For I clung to form, I clung to feeling, I clung to perception, I clung to formations, I clung to consciousness. Because of that clinging, there is becoming for me; because of becoming, birth; because of birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Thus is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.’”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 75 – Māgandiyasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, a woman, attending to her own female faculties, female deportment, female attire, female nature, female desires, female voice, female adornment — becomes lustful and…
item.description:
“Monks, a woman, attending to her own female faculties, female deportment, female attire, female nature, female desires, female voice, female adornment — becomes lustful and delights in them. Through being lustful and delighting in them, she attends to external male faculties, male deportment, male attire, male nature, male desires, male voice, male adornment, and becomes lustful and delights in them. Through being lustful and delighting in them, she desires external bonding. With that bonding as condition, pleasure and joy arise, and she desires that pleasure and joy. Monks, through delighting in their own femininity, beings become bonded to men. Thus, monks, a woman does not escape her own femininity.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.51
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Rādha, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving there is for form — abandon it. Thus that form will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made…
item.description:
“Rādha, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving there is for form — abandon it. Thus that form will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made non-existent, so that it cannot arise again in the future. Regarding feeling … perception … formations … Rādha, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving there is for consciousness — abandon it. Thus that consciousness will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made non-existent, so that it cannot arise again in the future.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 23.9

item.title: “‘Visible here and now, visible here and now (sanditthiko),’ venerable sir, is said. To what extent, venerable sir, is the Dhamma visible here and now,…
item.description:
“‘Visible here and now, visible here and now (sanditthiko),’ venerable sir, is said. To what extent, venerable sir, is the Dhamma visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise?” - “Here, Upavāna, having seen a form with the eye, a monk experiences the form but does not experience lust for the form, and there is no inner lust for forms. He knows: ‘There is no inner lust for forms in me.’ As long as, Upavāna, having seen a form with the eye, a monk experiences the form but does not experience lust for the form, and there is no inner lust for forms — he knows that — thus, Upavāna, the Dhamma is visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.70

item.title: Elder Hatthārohaputta: “This mind formerly wandered Wherever it wished, as it liked, as it pleased. Now I will restrain it thoroughly With wise reflection, As…
item.description:
Elder Hatthārohaputta:
“This mind formerly wandered
Wherever it wished, as it liked, as it pleased.
Now I will restrain it thoroughly
With wise reflection,
As a driver with a hook
Restrains a rutting elephant.”

From: Theragāthā 1.77
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “And how, monks, is a monk ‘washed clean’? He has washed away evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful…
item.description:
“And how, monks, is a monk ‘washed clean’? He has washed away evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful results, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Thus, monks, a monk is ‘washed clean.’”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 39 – Mahāhatthipadopamasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, just as a young man or woman, youthful, fond of adornment, would be distressed, ashamed, and disgusted if the carcass of a snake, a…
item.description:
“Monks, just as a young man or woman, youthful, fond of adornment, would be distressed, ashamed, and disgusted if the carcass of a snake, a dog, or a human were hung around their neck; so too, monks, that monk, examining the peril in those thoughts … the mind becomes steadied, settled, unified, and concentrated.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 20 – Vitakkasaṇṭhānasutta

item.title: “Monks, what are the defilements that should be abandoned by restraint? Here, a monk, reflecting wisely, lives with the restraint of the eye faculty. Monks,…
item.description:
“Monks, what are the defilements that should be abandoned by restraint? Here, a monk, reflecting wisely, lives with the restraint of the eye faculty. Monks, if he lives without restraining the eye faculty, harmful, feverish defilements might arise. If he restrains the eye faculty, those harmful, feverish defilements are no more. These, monks, are called the defilements that should be abandoned by restraint.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 2 – Sabbāsavasutta

item.title: “Fear, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. Suffering, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. Disease, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. A…
item.description:
“Fear, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. Suffering, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. Disease, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. A boil, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. A dart, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. Bondage, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. Mud, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. A womb, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures.
How, monks, is fear a synonym for sensual pleasures? Because those who are infected by sensual desire, bound by sensual lust, are not freed from fear in the present life, not freed from fear in the future — therefore fear is a synonym for sensual pleasures.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.56
